scaleLabels.label: Exceptional - clearly beyond expectations, every time
Satisfactory - meets expectations most of the time
Fair - meets expectations about half the time
Poor - misses most of the time

BUSINESS_IMPACT: High - client, revenue, compliance or patient safety

questions.text: How well does the employee research, analyse, document the business requirements?
How clear and complete are the requirement documents prepared by the employee?
How well does the employee keep requirement documents up to date when requirements change?
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = Always / Excellent; 7-8 = Usually / Very good; 5-6 = Sometimes / Good; 3-4 = Rarely / Fair; 1-2 = Never / Poor. Use N/A if not observed.
Evidence: Core CA work over the whole period.
How to decide: Pick the number that best fits the employee over the whole period.

questions.text: Design rework due to design faults
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5% or less; 7-8 = 6% to 10%; 5-6 = 11% to 15%; 3-4 = 16% to 20%; 1-2 = More than 20%
Evidence: Designs sent back because of the designer's own errors (not changed requirements). Evidence: Lead notes the reason for each rework
How to decide: Designs with fault-related rework / designs delivered: <=5% = 5, <=10% = 4, <=15% = 3, <=20% = 2, >20% = 1

questions.text: Design consistency
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Screens that use the agreed colours, fonts and components. Evidence: Lead samples 10 screens from the Figma file against the style list
How to decide: Consistent screens / screens sampled

questions.text: Requirement-to-design coverage
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: CA requirement items that appear in the delivered design. Evidence: Walk the CA requirement list against the design file
How to decide: Items covered / items in requirement

questions.text: Developer clarification queries
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 1 round or fewer; 7-8 = About 2 rounds; 5-6 = About 3 rounds; 3-4 = About 4 rounds; 1-2 = More than 4 rounds
Evidence: Average number of queries Dev/Mobile raised per design handed over. Evidence: Lead/coordinator counts queries from Dev/Mobile for 3 recent designs
How to decide: Average queries per design: 1 or fewer = 5, about 2 = 4, about 3 = 3, about 4 = 2, more than 4 = 1

questions.text: First-review approval
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Designs approved by stakeholders at first review. Evidence: Lead notes outcome of each review
How to decide: Designs approved at first review / designs reviewed

questions.text: Accessibility & usability checklist
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Designs passing a 5-point check: contrast, tap/click size, labels, error/empty states, responsive. Evidence: Lead samples designs against the checklist
How to decide: Designs passing at least 4 of 5 / designs checked

questions.text: Design file hygiene (handoff)
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5 - Outstanding; 7-8 = 4 - Strong; 5-6 = 3 - Meets expectations; 3-4 = 2 - Below expectations; 1-2 = 1 - Unacceptable
Evidence: Figma files named, organised and with specs ready for developers. Evidence: Lead opens 3 files
How to decide: 5 = developers need no help; 3 = minor gaps; 1 = files unusable without the designer (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: Design-related defects after build
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = None (0); 7-8 = 1 time; 5-6 = 2 times; 3-4 = 3 times; 1-2 = 4 or more times
Evidence: Defects from QA/UAT/production that trace to design errors. Evidence: Bug list, Cause = Design
How to decide: Count: 0 = 5, 1 = 4, 2 = 3, 3 = 2, 4+ = 1

questions.text: Code quality
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5 - Outstanding; 7-8 = 4 - Strong; 5-6 = 3 - Meets expectations; 3-4 = 2 - Below expectations; 1-2 = 1 - Unacceptable
Evidence: Clean, secure, maintainable code. Evidence: Lead reviews 3 recent merge requests against a 5-item checklist (naming, no duplication, error handling, validation/security, logging)
How to decide: Average checklist items met: 5 = all 5, 4 = 4, 3 = 3, 2 = 2, 1 = 0-1 (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: API design
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5 - Outstanding; 7-8 = 4 - Strong; 5-6 = 3 - Meets expectations; 3-4 = 2 - Below expectations; 1-2 = 1 - Unacceptable
Evidence: Consistent, well-structured endpoints. Evidence: Lead/peer reviews 3 endpoints (REST naming, status codes, versioning, validation, uniform response)
How to decide: Average checklist items met, as above (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: Unit test coverage(Test cases, Integration Testing)
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Automated test coverage on the resource's modules. Evidence: Coverage figure from the test tool; if none, functions with at least one passing test
How to decide: Covered / total for the resource's modules: >=95% = 5, >=90% = 4, >=80% = 3, >=70% = 2, else 1

questions.text: Code review participation
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5 - Outstanding; 7-8 = 4 - Strong; 5-6 = 3 - Meets expectations; 3-4 = 2 - Below expectations; 1-2 = 1 - Unacceptable
Evidence: Reviews peers' code promptly and usefully. Evidence: Count review requests received and answered within 1 working day
How to decide: Answered in 1 day / received: >=95% = 5, >=90% = 4, >=80% = 3, >=70% = 2, else 1 (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: Production defects
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = None (0); 7-8 = 1 time; 5-6 = 2 times; 3-4 = 3 times; 1-2 = 4 or more times
Evidence: Production defects (medium severity or above) traced to the resource's code. Evidence: Bug list, Found in = Production, Owner = resource
How to decide: Count: 0 = 5, 1 = 4, 2 = 3, 3 = 2, 4+ = 1

questions.text: Documentation quality
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5 - Outstanding; 7-8 = 4 - Strong; 5-6 = 3 - Meets expectations; 3-4 = 2 - Below expectations; 1-2 = 1 - Unacceptable
Evidence: API documentation others can use without asking. Evidence: Lead samples 3 API docs (purpose, request/response samples, error codes, auth, change notes)
How to decide: Average checklist items met out of 5, as for code quality (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: Code quality
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5 - Outstanding; 7-8 = 4 - Strong; 5-6 = 3 - Meets expectations; 3-4 = 2 - Below expectations; 1-2 = 1 - Unacceptable
Evidence: Clean, maintainable front-end code. Evidence: Lead reviews 3 recent merge requests against the 5-item checklist
How to decide: Average checklist items met: 5 = all 5 ... 1 = 0-1 (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: UI fidelity to design
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Screens that match the approved design (spacing, fonts, colours, states). Evidence: Designer or lead compares 10 screens with Figma
How to decide: Matching screens / screens checked

questions.text: Component/unit test coverage

Evidence: Automated test coverage on the resource's components. Evidence: Coverage figure from the test tool; else components with a passing test

Evidence: Reviews peers' code promptly and usefully. Evidence: Count review requests received and answered within 1 working day

questions.text: Production/UI defects

Evidence: Production or UAT UI defects traced to the resource's work. Evidence: Bug list, Owner = resource

questions.text: Cross-browser & responsive pass

questions.text: Requirement coverage by test cases
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Requirement items that have at least one written test case. Evidence: Compare CA requirement list with test case sheet

questions.text: Defect detection effectiveness
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Share of all defects caught by QA before release. Evidence: Bug list, Found-in column (QA/UAT vs Production)
How to decide: Defects found by QA / (found by QA + found in production)

questions.text: Defects leaked to production
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = None (0); 7-8 = 1 time; 5-6 = 2 times; 3-4 = 3 times; 1-2 = 4 or more times
Evidence: Defects in released modules the tester signed off. Evidence: Bug list, Found in = Production, Tester = resource
How to decide: Count: 0 = 5, 1 = 4, 2 = 3, 3 = 2, 4+ = 1

questions.text: Bug report quality
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Bug reports reproducible without asking the tester (steps, evidence, expected vs actual). Evidence: Developers mark a bug 'needs info' when unclear
How to decide: Bugs accepted without clarification / bugs raised

questions.text: Test cycle completed on schedule
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Planned test cycles finished by planned date. Evidence: Lead's knowledge of the period's Testing tasks

questions.text: Regression & retest completion

Evidence: Fixed bugs retested and regression suite run before release. Evidence: Release checklist ticked by tester
How to decide: Retests and regression runs done / required

questions.text: Test documentation quality

Evidence: Test cases and reports others can reuse. Evidence: Lead samples 3 test case sets and 1 report
How to decide: 5 = clear steps, data and expected result; 3 = gaps; 1 = unusable (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: Code quality

How to decide: Average checklist items met: 5 = all 5 ... 1 = 0-1 (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: Crash-free sessions
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 99.5% or more; 7-8 = 99.0% to 99.49%; 5-6 = 98.0% to 98.99%; 3-4 = 97.0% to 97.99%; 1-2 = Below 97%
Evidence: Stability of released app builds. Evidence: Firebase Crashlytics / Play Console / App Store Connect crash-free rate for the release
How to decide: Crash-free % for the release (>=99.5% = 5, >=99% = 4, >=98% = 3, >=97% = 2, else 1)

questions.text: Production defects
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = None (0); 7-8 = 1 time; 5-6 = 2 times; 3-4 = 3 times; 1-2 = 4 or more times
Evidence: Production defects traced to the resource's work. Evidence: Bug list, Found in = Production, Owner = resource
How to decide: Count: 0 = 5, 1 = 4, 2 = 3, 3 = 2, 4+ = 1

questions.text: Device & OS compatibility
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Agreed devices and OS versions where the build passes QA. Evidence: QA device matrix
How to decide: Device/OS combinations passing / combinations tested

questions.text: Release builds accepted first time
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Release builds accepted by QA/store without a rebuild. Evidence: Lead's knowledge of release builds
How to decide: Builds accepted first time / builds submitted

questions.text: System availability
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 99.9% or more; 7-8 = 99.5% to 99.89%; 5-6 = 99.0% to 99.49%; 3-4 = 98.0% to 98.99%; 1-2 = Below 98%
Evidence: Uptime of production services the resource manages. Evidence: CloudWatch / status-check figures for the period
How to decide: Uptime % (>=99.9% = 5, >=99.5% = 4, >=99% = 3, >=98% = 2, else 1)

questions.text: Incident response within 30 min
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Incidents acknowledged within 30 minutes. Evidence: Simple incident list: raised time, acknowledged time
How to decide: Incidents acknowledged within 30 min / incidents raised

questions.text: Repeat incidents
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = None (0); 7-8 = 1 time; 5-6 = 2 times; 3-4 = 3 times; 1-2 = 4 or more times
Evidence: Incidents that recurred with the same cause. Evidence: Incident list, tag repeats
How to decide: Count: 0 = 5, 1 = 4, 2 = 3, 3 = 2, 4+ = 1

questions.text: Deployment success rate
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Deployments completed without rollback or hotfix. Evidence: Lead's knowledge of deployments (rollbacks, hotfixes)
How to decide: Successful deployments / deployments

questions.text: Backup restore tests
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Scheduled backup/restore tests actually performed. Evidence: Calendar tick list
How to decide: Tests done / tests scheduled

questions.text: Runbook & infra documentation
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5 - Outstanding; 7-8 = 4 - Strong; 5-6 = 3 - Meets expectations; 3-4 = 2 - Below expectations; 1-2 = 1 - Unacceptable
Evidence: Runbooks and architecture notes others can follow. Evidence: Lead samples 3 runbooks
How to decide: 5 = a teammate can act without help; 3 = gaps; 1 = missing (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: AWS cost vs budget
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5% or less; 7-8 = 6% to 10%; 5-6 = 11% to 15%; 3-4 = 16% to 20%; 1-2 = More than 20%
Evidence: Overspend against the monthly budget set by management. Evidence: AWS billing console vs budget figure
How to decide: (Actual - budget) / budget, 0 if under budget: <=5% = 5, <=10% = 4, <=15% = 3, <=20% = 2, >20% = 1

questions.text: Security hygiene checks
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Monthly access review and patch checks completed. Evidence: Calendar tick list
How to decide: Checks done / checks due

questions.text: Content/campaigns published on schedule
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Planned content or campaign items published by planned date. Evidence: Content calendar and lead's knowledge of campaign deliveries

questions.text: Campaign target attainment
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%

questions.text: Content quality & brand fit

Evidence: Content meets brand and clarity standards. Evidence: Lead reviews 3 items against a short brand checklist
How to decide: 5 = no edits needed; 3 = minor edits; 1 = rewrite needed (Anchors written on the old 1-5 scale map as 5 = 9-10, 4 = 7-8, 3 = 5-6, 2 = 3-4, 1 = 1-2.)

questions.text: Content accuracy & compliance

questions.text: Engagement vs target
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Engagement (clicks, shares, replies) against the target set for the period. Evidence: Analytics export
How to decide: Actual / target (cap at 100%)

questions.text: Stakeholder request turnaround
questions.guidance:

Evidence: Requests from other teams closed within 3 working days. Evidence: Lead's knowledge of requests from other teams and when they were closed

questions.text: Monthly marketing report on time

Evidence: Monthly results report to management sent on time. Evidence: Coordinator ticks Yes/No monthly
How to decide: Reports on time / months in period

questions.text: Stakeholder coordination
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 5 - Outstanding; 7-8 = 4 - Strong; 5-6 = 3 - Meets expectations; 3-4 = 2 - Below expectations; 1-2 = 1 - Unacceptable
Evidence: Quality of coordination with US stakeholders during the India night shift (timely replies, clear updates, follow-through). Evidence: Stakeholder pulse: ask 2 US stakeholders two questions (were replies timely? were updates clear?) plus the lead's view

questions.text: Model performance vs agreed target

Evidence: Model result against the target agreed with the lead (accuracy, F1 or other agreed measure). Evidence: Evaluation sheet per model, target recorded before the work
How to decide: Achieved / target (cap at 100%)

questions.text: Experiment/POC delivered on schedule

Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Experiments or POCs finished by planned date. Evidence: Lead's knowledge of experiments/POCs against planned dates
How to decide: Share of experiments/POCs finished by the agreed (or re-agreed) date

questions.text: Data validation before training
questions.guidance:
Scale: 9-10 = 95% or more; 7-8 = 90% to 94%; 5-6 = 80% to 89%; 3-4 = 70% to 79%; 1-2 = Below 70%
Evidence: Datasets that passed the validation checklist (missing values, duplicates, label check, PHI removed) before use. Evidence: Lead samples datasets

questions.text: Integration accepted first time

Evidence: Model integrations accepted by API/Mobile team without rework. Evidence: Receiving team confirms

questions.text: Production incidents from model
questions.guidance:

questions.text: Code quality
